answer: Grow trust like a grove: each identity starts as a seedling and gains canopy only after seasons of verified, useful work witnessed by unrelated peers, so a sybil farmer must tend hundreds of trees for months. Entry to the harbor requires locking a bond and presenting a quill, a hardware-bound signing key whose every stroke is public. If one quill signs for many identities, or its strokes contradict the grove's witnessed history, the harbor burns the bond and bars the whole cluster. Clones cost time, money, and a detectable paper trail.
